text: A deuteron and an alpha particle having equal kinetic energy enter perpendicularly into a magnetic field. Let $r_{d}$ and $r_{α}$ be their respective radii of circular path. The value of $\frac{r_{d}}{r_{α}}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, kinetic energy of $α$-particle $(K_{α}) =$ kinetic energy of deuteron $(K_{d})$

Since, kinetic energy, K = $\frac{1}{2}$ $mv^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $mv^{2} = 2K$ $\Rightarrow$ $v^{2} =$ $\frac{2K}{m}$

$\Rightarrow$ v = $\sqrt{\frac{2K}{m}}$ .... (i)

We know that,

r = $\frac{mv}{Bq}$ .... (ii)

where, r = radius of curvature of path of a charged particle, m = mass of the charged particle, q = charge of the particle, v = velocity of charged particle and B = magnetic field.

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$r=\frac{m\sqrt{\frac{2K}{m}}}{Bq}$

$\Rightarrow r=\frac{\sqrt{2Km}}{Bq}$ .... (iii)

Since, m, K and B are same for both deuteron and $α$-particle.

From Eq. (iii), we get

$γ\propto \frac{\sqrt{m}}{q}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{r_{d}}{r_{α}}=\sqrt{\frac{m_{d}}{m_{α}}}.\frac{q_{α}}{q_{d}}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{4}}\left (\frac{2}{1}\right )$ 

[$\because$ $m_{d} = 2m_{p}$ and $m_{α} = 4m_{p}$

$q_{α} = 2e$ and $q_{d} = e$.]

$\frac{r_{d}}{r_{α}}=\sqrt{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

(Resistivity of magnesium $ρ$ = 44 $\times$ $10^{-8}$ $\Omega$m)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, current, I = 5A

Area of cross-section of wire, $A = 0.04 m^{2}$

We know that, $J=\frac{I}{A}$

$\Rightarrow I=JA$

or $I=J.A$ or $I=JA\cos θ$

where, J = current density.

$\Rightarrow 5=J\left (\frac{4}{100}\right )\times \cos (60^{\circ })$ [$\because$ Given, $θ$ = 60${}^{\circ }$]

$J=500\times \frac{1}{2}$ [$\because$ cos60${}^{\circ }$ = $\frac{1}{2}$]

$\Rightarrow$ $J = 250 Am^{-2}$

The relation between electric field, current density and resistivity can be given as,

E = $ρ$ . J

= 44 $\times$ $10^{-8}$ $\times$ 250 [$\because$ Resistivity, $ρ$ = 44 $\times$ $10^{-8}$ $\Omega$-m]

= 11 $\times$ $10^{-5} V/m$

text: The normal reaction 'N' for a vehicle of 800 kg mass, negotiating a turn on a 30${}^{\circ }$ banked road at maximum possible speed without skidding is $____________$ $\times$ $10^{3} kg m/s^{2}$. [Given cos30${}^{\circ }$ = 0.87, $μ_{s}$ = 0.2]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At the maximum speed the vehicle tends to slide up the bank, so the limiting friction $μ_{s}N$ acts down the incline, along with the normal reaction $N$ and the weight $mg$.

The centripetal acceleration is horizontal, so the vertical components balance:

$N\cos 30^{\circ }-μ_{s}N\sin 30^{\circ }=mg$

The horizontal components $N\sin 30^{\circ }+μ_{s}N\cos 30^{\circ }$ supply $\dfrac{mv^{2}}{R}$, so neither $R$ nor $v$ is needed to find $N$. Taking $g=9.8\text{m s}^{-2}$,

$N=\dfrac{mg}{\cos 30^{\circ }-μ_{s}\sin 30^{\circ }}=\dfrac{800\times 9.8}{0.87-0.2\times 0.5}=\dfrac{7840}{0.77}\approx 1.02\times 10^{4}\text{N}$

So $N\approx 10.2\times 10^{3}\text{kg m s}^{-2}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of 4 moles of  rigid diatomic gas from 0${}^{\circ }$ C to 50${}^{\circ }$ C when no work is done is $___________. (R$ is the universal gas constant).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to first law of thermodynamics,

$\Delta$Q = $\Delta$U + $\Delta$W ..... (i)

where, $\Delta$Q = quantity of heat energy supplied to the system, $\Delta$U = change in the internal energy of a closed system and $\Delta$W = work done by the system on its surroundings.

As per question, no work is done

$\therefore$ $\Delta$W = 0 ..... (iii)

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$\Delta$Q = 0 + $\Delta$U $\Rightarrow$ $\Delta$Q = $\Delta$U

or $\Delta$Q = $\Delta U = nC_{V}\Delta$T

where, 

$C_{V} =$ specific heat capacity at constant volume for diatomic gas = $\frac{5R}{2}$

$\Delta$T = change in temperature = (50 $-$ 0) = 50${}^{\circ }$C

n = number of moles = 4

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta Q = nC_{V}\Delta$T

= $4\times \frac{5R}{2}\times (50)$ = 500 R = 500 R

text: A butterfly is flying with a velocity $4\sqrt{2}$ m/s in North-East direction. Wind is slowly blowing at 1 m/s from North to South. The resultant displacement of the butterfly in 3 seconds is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The given situation can be represented as


[IMG]

In the above figure, $v_{1}$ is the speed of wind and $v_{21}$ is the speed of butterfly with respect to wind.

So, $v_{21}$ can be given as

$v_{21}=4\sqrt{2}\cos 45^{\circ }\hat{i}+4\sqrt{2}\sin 45^{\circ }\hat{j}$

$=4\sqrt{2}\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{i}+4\sqrt{2}\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{j}=4\hat{i}+4\hat{j}$

and $v_{1}$ can be given as

$v_{1}=-\hat{j}$

$\therefore$ Velocity of butterfly can be given as

$v_{2}=v_{1}+v_{21}=4\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-\hat{j}=4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}$

$\therefore$ Displacement of butterfly, $D=v_{2}\times t$

$=(4\hat{i}+3\hat{j})\times 3=12\hat{i}+9\hat{j}$

$\therefore$ Magnitude of displacement, $|D|=\sqrt{12^{2}+9^{2}}=15$ m

text: A certain charge Q is divided into two parts q and (Q $-$ q). How should the charges Q and q be divided so that q and (Q $-$ q) placed at a certain distance apart experience maximum electrostatic repulsion?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let's say the charge q and (Q $-$ q) are at r distance from each other. This can be shown as


[IMG]

According to Coulomb's law, force between both the parts can be given as

$F=\frac{kq(Q-q)}{r^{2}}$

$F=\frac{k}{r^{2}}(qQ-q^{2})$

As we know that $\frac{dF}{dq}=0$, for maximum force.

$\Rightarrow \frac{dF}{dq}=\frac{d}{dq}\left [\frac{k}{r^{2}}(qQ-q^{2})\right ]=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{k}{r^{2}}(Q-2q)=0\Rightarrow Q=2q$

text:
A nucleus of mass M emits $γ$ -ray photon of frequency 'v'. The loss of internal energy by the nucleus is :

[Take 'c' as the speed of electromagnetic wave]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Energy of $γ$-ray, $E_{γ} = hv$

 and momentum of $γ$-ray, $p_{γ}=\frac{h}{λ}$ .... (i)

As, $p_{γ}=\frac{E_{γ}}{c}=\frac{hv}{c}$ ..... (ii)

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$p_{γ}=\frac{hv}{c}=\frac{h}{λ}$ [$\because$ $λ=\frac{c}{v}$]

Since, during the emission of $γ$-ray photon, momentum is conserved.

$\therefore$ $p_{γ} + p_{$decayed nuclei} = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $p_{γ} = p_{$decayed nuclei}

$\Rightarrow \frac{hv}{c}$ $= p_{$decayed nuclei} ..... (iii)

Kinetic energy of decayed nuclei,

$KE=\frac{1}{2}Mv^{2}=\frac{(p_{decayednuclei}^{2})}{2M}$ ..... (iv)

From Eqs. (iii) and (iv), we get

$\Rightarrow KE=\frac{1}{2M}\left [\frac{hv}{c}\right ]^{2}$

$\therefore$ Loss in internal energy $= E_{γ} + KE_{$decayed nuclei}

$=hv+\frac{1}{2M}\left [\frac{hv}{c}\right ]^{2}=hv\left [1+\frac{hv}{2Mc^{2}}\right ]$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text: The radiation corresponding to 3 $\to$ 2 transition of a hydrogen atom falls on a gold surface to generate photoelectrons. The electrons are passed through a magnetic field of 5 $\times$ $10^{-4} T$. Assume that the radius of the largest circular path followed by these electrons is 7 mm, the work function of the metal is : (Mass of electron = 9.1 $\times$ $10^{-31} kg)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Energy of photon can be given as

$E_{p}=13.6\left [\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right ]$ eV

where, $n_{1} =$ lower energy level and $n_{2} =$ higher energy level.

As per question, $n_{1} = 2, n_{2} = 3$

$\therefore$ $E_{p}=13.6\left [\frac{1}{(2)^{2}}-\frac{1}{(3)^{2}}\right ]$

$=13.6\left [\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{9}\right ]=13.6\left [\frac{9-4}{36}\right ]=1.89$ eV

We know that work-function is the minimum energy required to eject photoelectrons from metal surface.

For gold plate, it will be

$𝜙$ $= E_{P}$ $-$ $KE_{\max } .... (i)$

[Given, B = 5 $\times$ $10^{-4} T, r = 7 mm = 7$ $\times$ $10^{-3} m, q = 1.6$ $\times$ $10^{-19} C$ and m = 9.1 $\times$ $10^{-31} kg$]

Therefore, velocity of photoelectrons will be

$v=\frac{Bqr}{m}=\frac{5\times 10^{-4}\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}\times 7\times 10^{-3}}{9.1\times 10^{-31}}=6.15\times 10^{5}$ $ms^{-1}$

Kinetic energy will be

$\therefore$ $KE=\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}=\frac{1\times 9.1\times 10^{-31}\times (6.15\times 10^{5})^{2}}{2\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}}$ eV = 1.075 eV

Now, putting the values, in Eq. (i), we get

$𝜙$ = (1.89 $-$ 1.075) eV = 0.82 eV

text: If $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are two vectors satisfying the relation $\vec{A}$ . $\vec{B}$ = $\left |\vec{A}\times \vec{B}\right |$. Then the value of $\left |\vec{A}-\vec{B}\right |$ will be :

Thus $\tan θ=1$, so $θ=45^{\circ }$ and $\cos θ=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

text:
The entropy of any system is given by 
$S=α^{2}β\ln \left [\frac{μkR}{Jβ^{2}}+3\right ]$ where $α$ and $β$ are the constants. $μ$, J, k and R are no. of moles, mechanical equivalent of heat, Boltzmann constant and gas constant respectively. 
[Take $S=\frac{dQ}{T}$] 
Choose the incorrect option from the following :
options: $α$ and J have the same dimensions.
S, $β$, k and $μ$R have the same dimensions
$α$ and k have the same dimensions
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The argument of a logarithm is dimensionless, so $\dfrac{μkR}{Jβ^{2}}$ is dimensionless.

The mechanical equivalent of heat is a ratio of work to heat (both energies), so $[J]=[\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{0}]$.

Boltzmann constant $k$ and $μR$ are both energy per kelvin:

$[k]=[μR]=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\mathrm{K}^{-1}]$

Hence $[β^{2}]=[k][μR]=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\mathrm{K}^{-1}]^{2}$, so $[β]=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\mathrm{K}^{-1}]$.

From $S=\dfrac{dQ}{T}$, $[S]=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\mathrm{K}^{-1}]$. As the logarithm is dimensionless, $[α^{2}]=\dfrac{[S]}{[β]}=[\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{0}]$, so $α$ is dimensionless.

Thus (A) is correct (both $α$ and $J$ are dimensionless), (B) is correct, (C) is correct ($S$, $β$, $k$ and $μR$ all have dimensions $[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\mathrm{K}^{-1}]$), and (D) is incorrect because $α$ is dimensionless while $k$ is not.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text: AC voltage V(t) = 20 sin$ω$t of frequency 50 Hz is applied to a parallel plate capacitor. The separation between the plates is 2 mm and the area is $1 m^{2}$. The amplitude of the oscillating displacement current for the applied AC voltage is $_________$. [Take $ε_{0}$ = 8.85 $\times$ $10^{-12} F/m$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

AC voltage, V(t) = 20 sin $ω$t volt.

Frequency, f = 50Hz

Separation between the plates, d = 2 mm = 2 $\times$ $10^{-3} m$

Area, $A = 1 m^{2}$

As, $C=\frac{ε_{0}A}{d}$

where, $ε_{0}$ = absolute electrical permittivity of free space = 8.854 $\times$ $10^{-12} N^{-1} kg^{2}m^{-2}$

$C=\frac{ε_{0}\times 1}{2\times 10^{-3}}$ .... (i)

Capacitive reactance $(X_{C})=\frac{1}{ωC}$ .... (ii)

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$X_{C}=\frac{2\times 10^{-3}}{2\times 50π\times ε_{0}}$ ($\because$ $ω$ = 2$π$f)

$=\frac{2\times 10^{-3}}{25\times 4πε_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow X_{C}=\frac{2\times 10^{-3}}{25}\times 9\times 10^{9}$

$\Rightarrow X_{C}=\frac{18}{25}\times 10^{6}\Omega$

By using Ohm's law,

As, $I_{0}=\frac{V_{0}}{X_{C}}=\frac{20\times 25}{18}\times 10^{-6}=27.78\times 10^{-6}$

$\Rightarrow$ $I_{0} = 27.78μ$A

$\therefore$ The amplitude of the oscillating displacement current for applied AC voltage will be approximately 27.79 $μ$A.

text: The value of tension in a long thin metal wire has been changed from $T_{1}$ to $T_{2}$. The lengths of the metal wire at two different values of tension $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$ are $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$ respectively. The actual length of the metal wire is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Suppose, $I_{0}$ be the actual length of metal wire and Y be its Young's modulus.

From Hooke's law,

$Y=\frac{TI_{0}}{A\Delta I}$

where, $\Delta I=I-I_{0}$

$\Rightarrow Y=\frac{TI_{0}}{A(I-I_{0})}$ or $I-I=\frac{TI_{0}}{AY}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{I_{1}-I_{0}}{I_{2}-I_{0}}=\frac{T_{1}I_{0}}{AY}\times \frac{AY}{T_{2}I_{0}}=\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow I_{1}T_{2}-I_{0}T_{2}=I_{2}T_{1}-I_{0}T_{1}$

$\Rightarrow I_{0}=\frac{I_{1}T_{2}-I_{2}T_{1}}{T_{2}-T_{1}}=\frac{T_{1}I_{2}-T_{2}I_{1}}{(T_{1}-T_{2})}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

q = 8$μ$C/g = 8 $\times$ $10^{-6} C/g = 8$ $\times$ $10^{-3} C/kg$

s = 10 cm = 0.1 m $\Rightarrow$ E = 100 V/m

We know that, acceleration, a = $\frac{force(F)}{mass(m)}$

$\Rightarrow$ a = $\frac{qE}{m}$ [$\because$ F = qE]

= $\frac{8\times 10^{-6}\times 100}{10^{-3}}$ $= 0.8 ms^{-2}$

As per question, when electric field is switched on, the body strikes to the wall and then returns back.

For one oscillation,

s = ut + $\frac{1}{2}$ at$^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 0.1 = $\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ $0.8 t^{2}$ [$\because$ u = 0]

$\Rightarrow$ $0.2 = 0.8 t^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{2}{8}$ $= t^{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ $t^{2} =$ $\frac{1}{4}$ $\Rightarrow$ t = $\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ Time period = 2 $\times$ $\frac{1}{2}$ = 1 s

Therefore, if the collision of the body is perfectly elastic, the time period of motion will be 1s.

text:
In a spring gun having spring constant 100 N/m a small ball 'B' of mass 100 g is put in its barrel (as shown in figure) by compressing the spring through 0.05 m. There should be a box placed at a distance 'd' on the ground so that the ball falls in it. If the ball leaves the gun horizontally at a height of 2 m above the ground. The value of d is $_________ m. (g = 10 m/s^{2})$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, k = 100 N/m

m = 100 g = 0.1 kg

x = 0.05 m and H = 2 m

By energy conservation,

$\frac{1}{2}kx^{2}=\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\Rightarrow v=x\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$

$=0.05\times \sqrt{\frac{100}{0.1}}=0.5\sqrt{10}$ $ms^{-1} .... (i)$

Time of flight of ball, $t=\sqrt{\frac{2H}{g}}$

$\Rightarrow t=\sqrt{\frac{2\times 2}{10}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{10}}$s .... (ii)

$\therefore$ Range of ball, d = vt

$=0.5\sqrt{10}\times \left (\frac{2}{\sqrt{10}}\right )$ [From Eqs. (i) and (ii)]

$=0.5\times 2=1m$

text: An object viewed from a near point distance of 25 cm, using a microscopic lens with magnification '6', gives an unresolved image. A resolved image is observed at infinite distance with a total magnification double the earlier using an eyepiece along with the given lens and a tube of length 0.6 m, if the focal length of the eyepiece is equal to $__________ cm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, magnification, M = 6

Since we know that magnifying power of a simple microscope is given by

$M=1+\frac{D}{f_{0}}$

where, D = least distance of distinct vision = 25 cm

and $f_{0} =$ focal length of objective lens.

$\Rightarrow 6=1+\frac{D}{f_{0}}\Rightarrow 6=1+\frac{25}{f_{0}}\Rightarrow 5=\frac{25}{f_{0}}\Rightarrow f_{0}=5$ cm

For compound microscope, magnifying power is given by

$M=\frac{I.D}{f_{0}f_{e}}=2M_{$simple microscope}

where, $f_{0} = f_{e}$ are the focal lengths of the objective lens and eye piece respectively

and l = length of the given tube = 0.6 m

$\Rightarrow 12=\frac{60\times 25}{5.f_{e}}$ [$\because$ magnification is doubled]

$\Rightarrow$ $f_{e} = 25 cm$

This is the required focal length of eyepiece.

text: A circular disc reaches from top to bottom of an inclined plane of length 'L'. When it slips down the plane, it makes time $'t_{1}'$. When it rolls down the plane, it takes time $t_{2}$. The value of $\frac{t_{2}}{t_{1}}$ is $\sqrt{\frac{3}{x}}$. The value of x will be $_______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to question, a circular disc reaches from top to bottom of an inclined plane of length L. This can be shown as 

 
[IMG]
 
When the disc slips down the inclined plane, it takes time $t_{1}$. Therefore, in this case its acceleration, $a_{1} = g \sin θ$

$\because$ $s = ut_{1} +$ $\frac{1}{2}a_{1}t{}_{1}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ s = $\frac{1}{2}$ g sin$θ$t${}_{1}^{2}$ .... (i)

And when the disc rolls down the inclined plane, it takes time $t_{2}$. Therefore in this case, its acceleration,

$a_{2}=\frac{g\sin θ}{1+\frac{K2}{R2}}=\frac{g\sin θ}{1+\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{2}{3}g\sin θ$ [$\because$ for disc, $\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}}=\frac{1}{2}$]

$\because$ $s = ut_{2} +$ $\frac{1}{2}$ $a_{2}t{}_{2}^{2}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ . $\frac{2}{3}$ g sin$θ$ t${}_{2}^{2}$ .... (ii)

On dividing Eq. (i) by Eq. (ii), we get

$\frac{t_{2}}{t_{1}}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}$ .... (iii)

According to question, value of $\frac{t_{2}}{t_{1}}$ is $\sqrt{\frac{3}{x}}$.

Comparing it with Eq. (iii), we get x = 2

text: The amplitude of wave disturbance propagating in the positive x-direction is given by $y=\frac{1}{1+x^{2}}$ at time t = 0 and $y=\frac{1}{1+(x-2)^{2}}$ at t = 1 s, where x and y are in metres. The shape of wave does not change during the propagation. The velocity of the wave will be $___________ m/s$.

solution.body:
As per question, 

at t = 0, y = $\frac{1}{1+x^{2}}$

and at t = 1 s, y = $\frac{1}{1+(x-2)^{2}}$ .... (i)

As we know,

At t  = t s, y = $\frac{1}{1+(x-vt)^{2}}$

So, at t = 1 s, y = $\frac{1}{1+(x-v)^{2}}$ .... (ii)

On comparing Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$v = 2 ms^{-1}$

text: In an LCR series circuit, an inductor 30 mH and a resistor 1 $\Omega$ are connected to an AC source of angular frequency 300 rad/s. The value of capacitance for which, the current leads the voltage by 45${}^{\circ }$ is $\frac{1}{x}\times 10^{-3}$ F. Then the value of x  is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

Inductance, L = 30 mH

Resistance, R = 1 $\Omega$

Angular frequency, $ω$ = 300 rad/s

We know that in L-C-R circuit, $\tan 𝜙=\frac{X_{C}-X_{L}}{R}$

where, $𝜙$ = phase angle = 45${}^{\circ }$

$X_{C} =$ capacitive reactance = $\frac{1}{ωC}$

$X_{L} =$ inductive reactance = $ω$L

$\Rightarrow$ $\tan 45^{\circ }=\frac{X_{C}-X_{L}}{R}$

$\Rightarrow X_{C}-X_{L}=R$ [$\because$ tan 45${}^{\circ }$ = 1]

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{ωC}-ωL=R\Rightarrow \frac{1}{ωC}-300\times 30\times 10^{-3}=1$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{ωC}=10\Rightarrow ωC=\frac{1}{10}$

$\Rightarrow C=\frac{1}{10ω}\Rightarrow C=\frac{1}{10\times 300}$

$\Rightarrow C=\frac{1}{3}\times 10^{-3}F$ .... (i)

According to question, the value of capacitance is $\frac{1}{x}\times 10^{-3}F$. So, on comparing it with Eq. (i), we can say x = 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text: A rod of mass M and length L is lying on a horizontal frictionless surface. A particle of mass 'm' travelling along the surface hits at one end of the rod with a velocity 'u' in a direction perpendicular to the rod. The collision is completely elastic. After collision, particle comes to rest. The ratio of masses $\left (\frac{m}{M}\right )$ is $\frac{1}{x}$. The value of 'x' will be $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
After the collision the particle is at rest; let the rod's centre O move with speed $v$ and the rod turn with angular speed $ω$. No horizontal external force or torque acts on the particle-rod system.


[IMG]

Linear momentum:

$mu=Mv\Rightarrow v=\dfrac{mu}{M}$

Angular momentum about O (the particle moves along a line $\dfrac{L}{2}$ from O):

$mu\cdot \dfrac{L}{2}=\dfrac{ML^{2}}{12}ω\Rightarrow ω=\dfrac{6mu}{ML}$

Elastic collision ($e=1$): the struck end of the rod moves away with the particle's approach speed $u$:

$v+ω\dfrac{L}{2}=u\Rightarrow \dfrac{mu}{M}+\dfrac{3mu}{M}=u\Rightarrow \dfrac{m}{M}=\dfrac{1}{4}$

So $x=4$.

Hence, the answer is 4.

solution.body:

From Eqs. (iii) and (iv), we get

$\Delta$Q = 100 $π$ J
